Traders warn Finance Bill will raise bread prices

Small traders in Nairobi have warned that the proposed 16% value added tax on bread will push the price of a 400g loaf above KES 70, hurting low-income households that already spend most of their income on food.

The National Treasury argues the measure is necessary to raise KES 346 billion and reduce borrowing. Treasury officials said the revenue will fund roads, hospitals and schools in the coming financial year.

The Kenya Association of Manufacturers said bakers would pass the cost to consumers. Opposition leaders called on MPs to reject the bill, saying Kenyans are already overtaxed.

Market vendor Mary Wanjiku said customers were already buying less. "If bread goes up again, people will stop buying," she said.
